FINAL PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS
Brain, left temporal lobe mass, biopsy:
Low-grade astrocytic neoplasm; see comment.
COMMENT:
The sections display a glial neoplasm with moderate cellularity, consisting of pleomorphic cells with hyperchromatic nuclei and variable eosinophilic cytoplasm. No mitotic activity or necrosis is observed. Eosinophilic granular bodies are absent on H&E staining.
Reticulin and PAS stains, along with immunohistochemical analysis, were conducted on block B1. The tumor is reticulin poor, lacking a reticulin network around cells. PAS stain does not reveal eosinophilic granular bodies. Neurofilament stain shows occasional entrapped axons. GFAP stain highlights scattered tumor cells, with most cells appearing negative. CD34 stain is diffusely positive. Ki-67 labeling index is less than 1%. BRAF-V600E immunohistochemistry shows weak staining, indeterminate between artifactual and true positivity.
The findings suggest a low-grade astrocytic neoplasm, with differential diagnosis including pilocytic astrocytoma (WHO grade I) versus pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma (WHO grade II). Compared to a previous biopsy (S14-56789), this specimen shows increased cellularity and nuclear pleomorphism but lacks Rosenthal fibers. The increased pleomorphism and CD34 positivity suggest pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, though the absence of eosinophilic granular bodies and reticulin meshwork is atypical.
A DNA-based melting curve assay for BRAF exon 15 is underway, results to follow from the USC Molecular Pathology Laboratory.
This case will also be reviewed by Dr. Lisa Monroe at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital for her expert opinion and testing for BRAF-KIAA1549 fusion, characteristic of pilocytic astrocytoma. Results will be included in an addendum.
Reviewed at USC Neuropathology Consensus Conference on 7/20/2015 with agreement among attendees including Drs. Smith and Johnson.

COMMENTS
Differential diagnosis includes pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma (WHO grade II) and pilocytic astrocytoma (WHO grade I). Pathology in 2015 suggests pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, though pilocytic astrocytoma would fit the 2014 biopsy.
Immunophenotype with sparse GFAP and widespread CD34 supports pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma (PXA). Large pleomorphic nuclei with pseudo-inclusions are more typical of PXA than pilocytic astrocytoma (PA). BRAF:p.V600E mutation can occur in both, but more frequent in PXAs. Diagnosis of PXA preferred despite tumor location, where PA is more common.
SUPPLEMENTAL CLINICAL PATHOLOGY DATA
Sequencing (MG15-890) shows BRAF:p.V600E mutation in tumor cells.
No KIAA1549-BRAF fusion transcript detected in RNA from tissue sections. Derivatives allowed testing of two (ex15:ex9 / ex16:ex9) of nine KIAA1549-BRAF fusion variants usually tested at SJCRH (MC-15-123).
By iFISH (FC-15-789), no BRAF rearrangement, BRAF duplication detected in 14% of tumor cells.
INTERPRETATION
Positive for BRAF duplication.
Negative for BRAF rearrangement.

FINAL PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS
A. Brain, right temporal lobe, "tumor," biopsy: Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, WHO grade II; see comment.
B. Brain, right temporal lobe, "recurrent tumor," biopsy: Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, WHO grade II; see comment.
COMMENT:
The sections display fragments of hypercellular tumor tissue and separate fragments of unaffected brain tissue, indicating a non-infiltrative process. Tumor cells exhibit abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and oval to irregular, elongated hyperchromatic nuclei. Numerous large, pleomorphic cells including multinucleated forms are observed. Scattered foamy "xanthomatous" cells are present. Rare mitoses, up to 3/10HPF, are noted. No evidence of necrosis or vascular proliferation suggesting a higher grade tumor is seen. Eosinophilic granular bodies are abundant throughout the specimen. These findings are consistent with pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, WHO grade II.
Immunohistochemical stains reveal tumor cells positive for GFAP and negative for synaptophysin. Reticulin stain indicates intercellular reticulin network surrounding tumor cells, supporting the diagnosis of pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma. MIB1 labelling index is focally up to 4%.
Prior specimens of this patient (S19-1234 and SD18-5678) were reviewed. Both specimens display scattered, moderately pleomorphic cells but lack eosinophilic granular bodies or other diagnostic features of pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma.
Dr. Emily Chen has reviewed this case and prior specimens on this patient and concurs with the diagnosis and interpretation.
